topics.label: Introduction to inflammation lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of infection recognition via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular criteria by which the innate immune system senses pathogens and cellular damage while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and inflammatory signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genetics, cellular localization, receptor families, and downstream activation pathways of pattern recognition receptors, including toll-like receptors and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Cellular dynamics and systemic consequences of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells trigger leukocyte recruitment and tissue extravasation, as well as the transition toward adaptive priming or severe systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the passive and active mechanisms that extinguish inflammation, guide tissue repair, and give rise to chronic inflammation or protective granuloma formation.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
